description:
The /fly HUD velocity readout (labelled 'Velocity' with a vis-viva ScienceChip) displays 'NaN km/s' throughout the entire transit to any outer-planet destination (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres, Vesta, Psyche, Bennu). The same NaN propagates through the velocity-arrow length, the data-helio-kms DOM attribute, and the SpacecraftInfoCard speed row.

Expected: The HUD shows a physically meaningful positive speed in km/s at every spacecraft position. For a Hohmann transfer to Jupiter (a = (1.0 + 5.203)/2 = 3.102 AU), the speed at Earth departure follows the vis-viva equation: v = √(µ·(2/r − 1/a))·AU/yr→km/s ≈ 38.5 km/s. The speed monotonically decreases toward arrival at the destination. The value is always finite and positive.

Acceptance criteria:
- The HUD velocity readout must never display 'NaN km/s' for any mission or plan that /fly can load. `Number.isNaN(heliocentricKms)` must be false on every frame of every transit. [code-invariant: NaN in a user-facing display is a crash — no document needed.]
- The transfer semi-major axis `aTransferAu` passed to `flyHeliocentricSpeed()` in the `$derived` must be derived from the actual destination's orbital radius, not hardcoded to Mars. Expected: `a = (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a) / 2` for non-Moon heliocentric missions. [repo-data: DESTINATIONS records at src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts:117-140 define `a` (semi-major axis) for every DestinationId. `activeDestination` is declared as `$state<DestinationId>('mars')` at fly/+page.svelte:300. Both are in scope at the `$derived` site.]
- The speed readout value must satisfy vis-viva bounds for the actual destination. For Jupiter at departure: `v = sqrt(4π² · (2/1.0 − 2/(1+5.203))) · 4.7404 ≈ 38.5 km/s`. For all destinations, the value must be finite and positive across the full [R_EARTH_AU, DESTINATIONS[id].a] distance range. [spec: ADR-030 §'Trajectory math' / fly-physics.ts:L27-41 — vis-viva is the canonical formula. The function itself is sound; the call site at fly/+page.svelte:952 feeds it the wrong transfer a.]

Domain facts:
- Jupiter semi-major axis: 5.203 AU (DESTINATIONS.jupiter.a via static/data/planets.json)
- Saturn semi-major axis: 9.537 AU
- Mars semi-major axis: 1.524 AU (the value currently hardcoded into the speed call site)

Target: src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — line 952 — the second argument (aTransferAu) of the `flyHeliocentricSpeed(scR, ...)` call inside the `$derived heliocentricKms` expression. The hardcoded `R_MARS_AU` must be replaced with the destination's actual semi-major axis from `DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a`.
Do NOT change src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — it is not the owner of this symptom.
